subject: Post-call: invoice & billing requirements — PO vs card, net terms, marketplace
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>, Tom Grant <tom.grant@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: invoice & billing requirements — PO vs card, net terms, marketplace

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few asks so procurement can move forward: 

Recap
- Acme is interested in Redwood Dedicated for your research workloads with an initial commitment for Q3.
- Key procurement questions: whether we can accept PO vs credit card, net terms, invoice format (PDF vs XML/EDI), tax/VAT handling, and billing address/remit details. Also asked about AWS Marketplace as an alternative purchase path.

What we need from Acme
1) Confirm whether procurement will issue a PO or prefer to pay by card for initial purchase.
2) If PO: billing address, remit-to, and any required PO language.
3) Do you need Net30/Net45? Are there internal credit approvals required?
4) Invoice delivery preference: PDF via email, SFTP, or EDI/XML?
5) Any tax-exempt status / VAT requirements or special supplier forms we should fill out.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-acme-2026-06-30.pdf (pricing + SOW) — I also attached a sample invoice format for reference.

Next steps
- If you plan to issue a PO, please send the billing address and PO sample (or the PO itself) and we'll route to Finance for set-up.
- If you want to purchase via AWS Marketplace, let us know and we'll confirm listing/contracting flow.

I've looped in Rishi for onboarding questions and Dev in finance to expedite vendor setup once we have the PO.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: invoice & billing requirements — PO vs card, net terms, marketplace

Hi Samantha —

Great — thanks for the clarity. Answers below and next steps: 

1) PO vs Card: We can accept a PO. For Net terms (Net30) we require standard vendor onboarding and a credit approval from Finance. In practice we can provision service while finance processes the credit (subject to internal approvals) or set an initial prepayment if needed to expedite.

2) Vendor docs: attached vendor_docs.zip contains our W9, Redwood tax ID, and supplier form. If you need an alternative format (vendor portal link), let me know.

3) Invoice delivery: We can send invoices as PDF to ap@acmehealth.com. We also support SFTP/automatic EDI/XML exports for customers that require that format — implementation typically happens during onboarding.

4) Tax / VAT: For US-based Acme, we will apply standard US sales tax rules — if you are tax-exempt, please provide the certificate and we will mark the account accordingly. For international VAT scenarios we have a separate flow.

5) Marketplace: We can support purchase via AWS Marketplace for Redwood Hosted; Dedicated purchases via Marketplace are possible depending on the listing/metering — we'll confirm with Product/Marketplace team if you prefer that route.

Next steps (proposed):
- Samantha / Tom: please send the official PO and billing/remit details when available (or indicate marketplace interest).
- Dev (cc'd): once we have PO, please trigger vendor onboarding/credit check and confirm expected timeline for Net30 availability.
- Rishi: please confirm onboarding steps and timing for Dedicated provisioning once billing is in place.

Thanks — attaching vendor docs and the proposal again.

Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: vendor_docs.zip, redwood-proposal-acme-2026-06-30.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:30:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: invoice & billing requirements — PO vs card, net terms, marketplace

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the heads up. A few internal notes for routing once we receive the PO: 
- Please ask Acme to include remit-to address and the exact billing name used for tax ID matching. Mismatched names slow down vendor onboarding.
- We can approve Net30 for customers after a standard credit review (48-72 business hours once we have PO + supplier form + W9). For larger commitments we may require an initial deposit or signed commitment confirming the spend.
- Ask procurement whether they require invoices to include a specific PO field (e.g., "Cost Center") or GL code — if yes, we can include custom fields on the invoice PDF.
- If they want Marketplace purchase, note that Marketplace billing will go through AWS and Redwood will invoice/settle per AWS terms; that changes invoicing flow and sometimes delays credit applicability. If Acme prefers Net terms, direct PO / direct contract is usually faster.

I'll be on standby to kick off vendor set-up once we have the PO and completed supplier form.

—Dev
Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
